title: Event synchronization, snapshotting, and gap-healing for SSE streaming
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Clients consuming long-running server-sent events (SSE) can lose events during transient connection failures. Current reconnect behavior relies on resume tokens and naive replays which can lead to hole windows, duplicate processing, or excessive replays for high-throughput channels. We need a pragmatic, backward-compatible mechanism to ensure event continuity (no silent gaps) while keeping bandwidth and server CPU reasonable for high-frequency streams.
goals: 1) Provide deterministic gap detection and recovery for SSE consumers. 2) Keep changes minimally intrusive to existing event formats and client implementations. 3) Allow progressive rollout and opt-in negotiation so older clients continue to work. 4) Provide observability and SLOs for resumed streams and data loss rates.
proposal_summary:
Introduce lightweight periodic 'stream snapshots' and a per-chunk Sequence/Range+Checksum header, plus a small 'partial-ack' exchange during reconnect that allows the server to efficiently heal gaps without full replay. Key ideas:
- Each event chunk includes metadata headers: seq_start, seq_end, chunk_id, and chunk_checksum. These are encoded as header fields inside the SSE 'event:' line or a compact JSON prefix for binary-safe payloads.
- Server emits a compact snapshot event every N seconds or M bytes with the latest committed sequence number and an optional short recent-event index (last K seq numbers + offsets). Snapshot frequency configurable per route.
- On reconnect, client supplies Last-Observed-Seq and an optional Last-K list; server responds with a narrow repair window (missing seq ranges) and emits only missing events, or a snapshot if the window is too large.
- For safety, all emitted events retain idempotent dedup IDs so clients can safely dedupe duplicates.
- Backcompat: Feature negotiation header (X-Redwood-SSE-Ext: snapshot=1;ack=1;v=1). If absent, server falls back to current resume-token behaviour.
server_changes:
- Add chunk metadata embedding in SSE encoder path; opt into compact JSON prefix when payloads contain newlines or binary.
- Snapshot writer: periodic job per stream that writes snapshot events into the outgoing stream buffer (configurable interval).
- Reconnect handler: on incoming connection, parse X-Redwood-Client-Seq header and Last-K list; compute minimal repair window using stream index/commit log; return HTTP 200 with a small preface event indicating repair plan.
- Storage/retention: keep a short in-memory/trickle-backed index of recent sequence ranges per stream (configurable retention, e.g., 5 minutes or 10k events) to avoid disk IO for normal cases.
- Metrics: counters for repaired_windows, snapshot_emitted, repair_failures, average_repair_size, and percent_exceed_retention.
client_changes:
- Parse chunk metadata and attach seq bookkeeping.
- On disconnect, persist last-observed seq to local durable store (optionally memory for stateless clients).
- On reconnect, send X-Redwood-Client-Seq and optional Last-K list (comma-separated seq ids).
- Handle server preface: either apply narrow repair stream or accept a snapshot to reset state.
- Implement idempotent dedupe: use dedup IDs or sequence ranges to ignore duplicates.
- Fallback: if server responds with no support, continue to older resume-token flow.
tradeoffs_and_constraints: - Pros: deterministic gap recovery, much lower full-replay frequency for noisy networks, explicit metrics for repair success.\n- Cons: Slightly more bytes on wire for metadata and periodic snapshots; added server memory for short-term indexes; more complexity in encoder/decoder logic.\n- Rollout complexity: must support mixed-version clients/servers; negotiation header reduces risk but we'll still need to test cross-version edge cases (older client -> new server; new client -> old server).
compatibility_strategy:
- Add negotiation header X-Redwood-SSE-Ext.
- Server supports both modes concurrently (legacy resume-token and new snapshot/repair flow).
- Canary rollout: enable snapshot mode by default on internal canary hosts and expose as opt-in per-route flag in console.
- Docs: update streaming compatibility guide and SDK helpers (Node/Python) to expose reconnection helpers and dedupe primitives.
metrics_and_alerting: - track: percent_reconnects_with_gap, median_repair_size, repair_fail_rate.\n- Alerts: repair_fail_rate > 1% over 5m for high-throughput routes; pct_reconnects_with_gap > 2% for top-10 customer routes.\n- Dashboards: add a 'stream continuity' dashboard per-route showing snapshots emitted, recent repair windows, and average latency of repairs.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for encoder/decoder metadata.
- Integration test: simulated network flaps with artificial packet drops to verify minimal repair windows and dedupe.
- Load test: ensure snapshot emission and in-memory index scales to 100k concurrent streams with typical event rate.
- Backcompat regression tests: old client vs new server and new client vs old server matrix.
- Security: fuzz test the snapshot preface parser for header injection and large header denial-of-service.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge server+client feature gate behind runtime flag. 2) Internal canary (infra) for 72h, monitor repair_fail_rate and CPU/memory. 3) Gradual enablement for 10% of routes for 1 week. 4) Widen to 50% then 100% after two successful cycles. 5) Turn on default snapshot frequency reductions for high-throughput routes based on observed overhead.

comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Spike complete. Prototype shows 30-45% reduction in full replay traffic on noisy networks. Kept metadata prefix to < 80 bytes on average for text workloads.

2026-02-26 Arjun Patel: Implemented server-side snapshot writer and in-memory index. Pushed initial PR (server#5142). Performance note: index memory scales with avg stream depth; we need a configurable retention cap per route.
2026-03-01 Design review (Priya Rao): Approved the compact JSON prefix approach for binary-safe streams; asked to add explicit examples for SDKs. Action: Arjun to add examples in SDK PR.

2026-03-04 QA (Liam Gomez): Found race when snapshot emits during a manual checkpoint flush; added unit test and fixed ordering by serializing snapshot emission after checkpoint completion. PR updated.

2026-03-07 Security review (Elena Park): No high-risk issues; recommended hard limits on header sizes and a validation step for client-supplied Last-K lists to avoid forged long lists. Implemented size caps in reconnect handler.
2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Client helper PR opened (sdk#782) with Node and Python reconnection helpers. Need cross-language review from SDK owners before merging.
2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Preparing canary rollout config in console: route flag 'enable_snapshot_repair' and a per-route snapshot_interval_ms. Targeting canary start 2026-03-15.
